## Interfaces  for  asynchronous  images

The java.awt.Image class provides three interfaces - ImageProducer, ImageConsumer and  ImageObserver - which provide programmers with a consistent environment for creating and  processing Image data during real-time animation. One of the methods  createImage provided by the Component class is based on the ImageProducer and passes it  initial graphics data for Image. ImageProducer methods for drawing and preparation  images  require  to  ImageConsumer  sent  them  data  about  pixels  Images.

The ImageObserver watches the process and receives updates from the ImageProducer when new  data  become available.

Some implementations of these interfaces are provided in the Java API. We will briefly describe  interfaces and then move on to their specific implementations in the next section. Medium  the programmer will never need to implement these interfaces, but it is important to understand that  actually  going on  to  use images effectively.

The ImageProducer interface must be implemented by classes that can produce  data for Image. ImageProducer can be used as a parameter to the createImage method  Component class. ### Color  models

Having received an array of pixels, we must do something with it. Each pixel is represented by  this array as a single integer. It is necessary to extract from this integer all the data,  which we need to draw or otherwise interpret the pixel. Location  each pixel in the image can be inferred from the position in the array, and we use  Class  ColorModel,  to  interpret  whole  number  directly  how  color.

Almost any color can be represented as a unique combination of shades of red,  blue and green. There are other combinations based on other color sets, but  they are used exclusively in computer graphics. Almost all color monitors  get each pixel from a combination of red, blue and green dots. The ColorModel class is not  only allows us to parse the integers in the pixel array and split each one into  red, blue and green components, but also determine the degree of transparency. Component  transparency controls the output of the pixel: if the pixel is transparent, the background color is converted to  the displayed color of the pixel. On fig. Figure 9-2 shows the overlay of a partially transparent  Images  to opaque.

### Filtration  images

Now we can create images directly at the bit level, without  using the graphics primitives provided by the Graphics class. We can even  to manage  images,  loaded  from  networks;  from  help  Pixel Grabber  we  Can  receive  pixel values from the array. We can reverse the process using the class  MemoryImageSource. The Java API provides two classes designed specifically for this  tasks,  -FilteredImageSource  And  ImageFilter.

The FilteredImageSource class implements the ImageProducer interface. It takes an ImageProducer and  ImageFilter as construct parameters. By creating an image, he receives data about  pixels from the ImageProducer defined in the construct. Then changes this data  in a consistent manner dictated by the ImageFilter and sends the modified data  back via ImageConsumer. The ImageFilter class implements the ImageConsumer interface. He is not  changes pixel data. The Java API provides two simple extensions that allow  insert  color  filter  or  cut some  area for  new  Images.

The RGBImageFilter class does not perform any color filtering by default, but  transforms the pixel value and ColorModel used by the image for the specified  default RGB color model. To make it filter colors, we need to extend  method  filterRGB  this  class  for  fulfillment  necessary  US  filtration.  Consider  example,  which removes from  images all red  color.

Example  9-3.  Filter  removal  red  colors.

import  java.awt.image.*;

public class NoRedFilter extends RGBImageFilter {  public  int  filterRGB(int  x,  int  y,  int  rgb)  {

int  alpha  =  (rgb  &  0xff000000)>>24;  int red = (rgb & 0x00ff0000)>>16;  int green = (rgb & 0x0000ff00)>>8;  int  blue  =  (rgb  &  0x000000ff);

return  ((alpha<<24)|(green<<8)|(blue));

}

}

First, we explode the integer rgb variable by specifying the color of the pixel in the given array.  default RGB color scheme, and then add transparency, green and blue components  back to an RGB value, completely ignoring the red value. Please note that, so  as we are passing the x and y coordinates, we could change the filter color based on  location, but for our simple filter, this is useless. RGBColorFilter class - handy  filter that you can develop for your own needs, because in case  need  is he  performs  transformation  to  given  on  default  models  colors  RGB.

The CropImageFilter class is as simple as possible to use; you don't need to expand it,  to crop your images. Instead, you simply define the area you want  cut when building the filter. Method  int  hashCode()

This method, like the two just described, must always be overridden. If  this  not  do,  Class  will  impossible  use  jointly  from  class  java.util.hashtable,  discussed in chapter 6 . In order to learn how to construct a method, and in order to  understand,  why  is he  redefined,  Let's  consider  more  structure  hash tables.

Search speed is one of the main advantages of hash tables. The hash table never  looks through the contents of all key fields when searching. To find a component in a table,  consisting of N key-value pairs, it is necessary to perform a total of N comparison operations. IN  Java means that you need to call the comparison method N times. If N is enough  great,  extraction  element  from  tables  maybe  take  at  systems  tangible  number  time.

Instead, the hash table only performs a single comparison operation. It's getting  possible due to the special principle of storing its elements. Each key-value pair  placed in the basket. There can be several pairs in one basket, but, as a rule, in  only one such pair is stored in the basket. When the hash table is passed the key by which to  return a value, she asks herself, "Which bin should I place this key in?"  The table looks into a suitable basket and compares the passed key with the keys  being  in  basket.  How  less  keys in  basket,  topics  more efficient  Search.

How does a hash table decide which bucket to put a key/value pair in? For this  used  special  algorithm  -  hash function  (hash  function).  Her  a task  -  place  couples  "key-value" for the maximum number of baskets and thus simplify  further search, reducing the number of keys in one basket to a minimum. As a rule, when  this  respected  principle: basket  more,  how  steam  key-value".

This is where the hashCode method comes into play. As arguments to the hash function included in  composition  java.util.hashtable,  transmitted  whole  numbers.  whole  numbers  necessary  because,  what  in  the same hash table can store keys of different types. We have already talked briefly about the use of threads in the Java language. Java handles threads  in a very elegant way: it is the first popular language to include streams in  language specification. Java, as a powerful networking language, should have been able to  perform multi-threaded operations. The inclusion of threads makes Java a unique language  development of programs for the Internet.

Why are threads so useful? Imagine that you are creating a spreadsheet program and  want user input results to be processed in the background. In normal  single-threaded program, to get this result you would have to use  some  enough  confused  tricks  -  for example,  cycle,  which the  checks  input  from  keyboards  and if there is no input, it does some calculations. This solution is not very elegant, but it  could  would work.

But your decision becomes less and less crisp and clear when, later in the development of the project,  someone asks for background mode for a print routine, and someone else asks for  autosave. Now you have to fiddle more and more with these additional  routine operations that need to be performed between keystrokes. Your input loop with  keyboard quickly becomes confusing and cluttered, and it's all because you have  only  one thread of execution.

Of course one could use someone else's library which provides  support for multiple concurrently executing threads. This is possible, but far from  optimal. Whenever there is a change in a work project, you may need to  encounter ever new multithreading support libraries and learn new APIs.  Developers  Java  understood  this  And  performed support  flows  in  specifications  language.

Using the Java standard streams, we can solve our problems with the e-program.  tables are much easier. Each new task is executed as a separate thread. We are no longer  you need to pore over each new feature. Support for threads in the language helps and  creation  built-in  garbage collector.

This chapter focuses on how Java implements threading and the issues  programs,  using  lots of  streams.  If  you  yet  few  worked  from  multithreading,  this  chapter,  except  Togo,  maybe  change  your  representation  about  programming  at all.

The transition from one large program to a program made up of small threads has  radical meaning. Along the way, there are pitfalls to avoid and concepts  which need to be thought through. So let's dive into how Java creates and executes  multiple streams.

# Creation  flows  at  help  interface  runnable

What if we didn't want to extend the Thread class in the example above? Maybe,  We already have  eat  Class,  functional  opportunities  whom  we are quite satisfied  And we  we just want it to run as a separate thread. The answer is simple: use an interface  runnable.  Interfaces  Java  we  discussed  in  chapter  3 ,  "Objective  orientation  in  java".  Interfaces  provide a good way to define a set of standard functionality for  executable class. The Runnable interface implements one method, run, which is very similar to  work  class  thread.

Imagine that we have an outputClass that we want to turn into a stream. Everything, that  we  should  do,  -  this  implement  interface  runnable,  creating  shared  method  run.

Example  11-2.  Usage  interface  runnable.

class  outputClass  implements  runnable  {  String  name;

outputClass(String s) {  name  =  s;

}

public  void  run()  {

for(int i=0; i < 3; i++) {  System.out.println(name);  Thread.yield();

}

}

}

class  runThreads  {

public  static  void  main(String  argv[])  {

outputClass out1 = new outputClass("Thread 1");  outputClass out2 = new outputClass("Thread 2");  Thread  t1  =  new  Thread(out1);

Thread  t2  =  new  Thread(out2);  t1.start();

t2.start();

}

}

This example is functionally equivalent to example 11-1, but is implemented differently. we are here  create two instances of the outputClass class. These could be any classes, but they must  implement the Runnable interface. We then create two new threads and pass them to  created  copies  outputClass.  After  this  we  getting started  performance  flows  how  usually.

The difference between the two examples is in the constructor's call to the Thread class. In the first  example, we called the Thread(String) constructor, in the second - Thread(Runnable). We could  also call the Thread(Runnable, String) constructor. The Thread class has the following  constructors:

*   Thread()
*   Thread  (string)
*   Thread(Runnable)
*   Thread  (string,  runnable)
*   Thread  (thread group,  string)
*   Thread  (thread group,  runnable)
*   Thread(ThreadGroup,  runnable,  string)

## Planning  flows

The order in which the threads will execute and the amount of time they will receive from  processor, are the main questions for the developer. Each thread must share the CPU  time  from  others.  We  not  want  to  one  flow  monopolized  kiss  system.  Planning  threading is closely related to two concepts: unloading and time slicing. Let's Explore  each  concept  more.

A system that deals with multiple threads running can be either  priority or non-priority. Priority systems ensure that at any time  will  be carried out  flow  from  most  high  priority.  Everyone  streams  in  system  attributed  priority. The class variable Thread.NORM_Priority contains the value of the thread priority according to  by default. Thread class has setPriority and getPriority methods to set and define  priority. Using the setPriority method, you can change the priority of a thread for a virtual  Java machines. This method takes as an argument some integer in the range  valid values specified by two class variables Thread.MIN_PRIORITY and  Thread.MAX_PRIORITY.

The Java Virtual Machine is a priority, that is, the thread with  highest priority. Let's change the priority of the thread in the Java machine to the most  tall. After that, the thread will receive all the CPU time until it runs out or  put into a waiting state - possibly by the sleep command. But what will happen to  threads having the same priority? Let's take an example to see  behavior  Java.

How threads of the same priority are executed is not described in the Java specification.  It would seem that the threads should share the processor, but this is not always the case.  Order  them  fulfillment  determined  basic  operating room  system  And  hardware  means.  Obviously, on systems with a single processor, we cannot expect simultaneous execution  more than one thread. The operating system services threads with  planner,  which defines  execution order.

Let's take a closer look at what happened when we ran our program on  Sun car. The first thread ran to completion, then thread 2 did so, and finally  thread 3\. But if the first thread never ends, threads 2 and 3 will never  be performed. Of course, this causes some problems. The thread with the highest priority  will always run, while lower priority threads, depending on  operating system may not be able to run. If we need some  ordering, or even just sequential execution of threads, we will have to  do some  work.

The yield method provides a simple workaround for the time slicing problem. If  the yield method is used, the thread will voluntarily yield to the processor, which will give other threads  the ability to also get the processor time. Voluntary transfer of control especially  important in long cycles. Let's rewrite the previous program using the method  yield.

Java provides a mechanism for protecting variables in a program. The problem boils down to two  threads trying to perform some operation at the same time. We need one  a thread waited for another to finish. The operation could include several commands. These  commands  called  critical  section.  Critical  chapter  -  this  that  part  code,  which  must be protected so that the system does not fail. In our case with trains  the critical section is in the step method. The train must not be allowed to enter the track at that  time,  when that  already taken.

We can create a trainSwitch class that will protect our switch. It will contain two  method  -  lock  (blocking)  And  unlock  (unlock).  Entering  on the  dangerous  way,  train  must  call lock. As soon as the train leaves the track, it calls unlock. All other trains before  entry  on the  this way  have to wait  while he  not  will  unlocked.

In Java, critical sections of code are marked with the synchronyzed keyword. Any block  code can be marked as synchronized, but methods are usually marked that way. Tagging  parts  method  how  synchronized  actually  is an  example  bad  programming.

Programmers need to be aware of areas that can cause multithreading problems;  if you don't mark the method as synchronized people will need some code to figure out if  what is going on. For this reason, we use the synchronyzed keyword only on  level  method.

So what's the point of marking a method as synchronized? Associated with each class  one  monitor.  When  called  synchronized  method,  is he  checks  monitor.  If  Class  already blocked, the calling routine will wait. This means that at one point in time  only one thread will be in the critical block. Let's see how it is  is being implemented.

Example  11-7c. Class  trainSwitch.

class trainSwitch extends Thread {  protected boolean inUse=false;  public  synchronized  void  lock()  {

while (inUse) {  try  wait();

catch  (InterruptedException  e);

}

inUse  =  true;

}

public synchronized void unlock() {  inUse  =  false;

notify();

}

}

The trainSwitch class has two synchronized methods, lock and unlock, which protect  inUse variable of this class. We want to make sure that at any given time only  one thread is using the switch. The state of the switch is set in a boolean  variable. When the train uses the switch, inUse is set to true. Any  other trains wishing to use the switch will have to wait until the boolean  variable  not  will be reset  to false.

IN  example  11-7b  used  two  new  method,  wait  And  notify.  They are  serve  two  goals.

Their first task is to resolve a difficult situation. What would happen if in the above  example was the wait statement missing? The blocking routine would be in a loop and  occupied  monitor  for  class.  AND  then  none  would  not  smog  call  method  unlock,  to whom  also  needed  monitor.

Methods  wait  And  notify  are used,  to  solve  this  problem.  Method  wait  makes  flow  expect some event. Meanwhile, the monitor is released. This allows you to perform  other routines that need a class monitor. When control returns from  wait method, the monitor is also restored. The rest of the critical section is still  protected.

### Semaphores:  protection  others  public  resources

In previous examples, we used monitors to protect variables. Let's  expand  this  concept  before  any  general  resource.  We  wanted  would  protect  any  resource  systems,  which can be shared by multiple threads. An example of such a public resource  is a file. Two threads writing to the same file at once generate garbageHaving;  a situation where one thread is reading a file while another thread is writing to it, too  dangerous.  US  needed  some way  protection  integrity  our  file.

To protect files, you can apply concepts similar to those we used for  protecting the train switch in our last example. This type of protection is called  exceptional  blocking.  Only  one  flow  maybe  to read  or  change  meaning  in  one  moment of time. If we are dealing with files, especially infobase files  data, we generally do more reads than writes. We can  use this fact  to improve  our  the code.

Let's say we have a database of employees. It contains information such as addresses  and phone numbers. These values sometimes change, but more often they are read. US  we need to protect the data from distortion, but we want the program to be so  as efficient as possible. Instead of only exclusive locks, we use  a read lock and a write lock. We can have as many readers as we need,  but when someone wants to write something to a file, they must acquire an exclusive lock.  This  concept  wears  semaphore name  (semaphore).

What  necessary  for  creation  this  semaphore?  We  want  allow  streams  free  to read  file,  but assume that when some thread wants to change the information, it should become  the only working  with base  data  flow.

Our semaphore has four states. In the first, empty one, no thread reads or  writes information. We can accept both read and write requests, and they can  be serviced immediately. The second state is the read state. Here we have some  the number of threads reading from the database. We count the number of readers, and if it  the number becomes zero, we return to the empty state. The write request must  wait. We can only enter the write state from an empty state. All reader threads  should  to be  completed,  And  no others  streams  can not  write down  in  file.  Any  requests  about  reading  or  records  should  wait  completion  this  flow.  Any  flow  in  able  expectations  must wait for the thread in the write state to terminate before exiting this  states. When the write request completes, we return to an empty state. When  a notify message has been sent, the waiting thread can be serviced. Below is the code,  providing  this semaphore.

Example  11-8a.  Semaphore.

class  Semaphore  {

final static int EMPTY = 0;  final  static  int  READING  =  one;  final  static  int  WRITING  =  2;  protected int state=EMPTY;  protected  int  readCnt=0;

public synchronized void readLock() {  if  (state  ==  EMPTY)  {

state  =  READING;

}

else  if  (state  ==  READING)  {

}

else if (state == WRITING) {  while(state  ==  writing)  {

try  wait();

catch  (InterruptedException  e);

}

state  =  READING;

}

readCnt++;  return;

}

public  synchronized  void  writeLock()  {

if  (state  ==  EMPTY)  {

state  =  WRITING;

}

else  {

while(state  !=  EMPTY)  {

try  wait();

catch  (InterruptedException  e);

}

}

public  synchronized  void  readUnlock()  {  readCnt--;

if  (readCnt  ==  0)  {

state = EMPTY;  notify();

}

}

public  synchronized  void  writeUnlock()  {  state  =  EMPTY;

notify();

}

}

### Prevention  dead ends

You can now synchronize the work of multiple threads and make sure that they  save public resources. You started experimenting with multiple  flows - and suddenly the system hangs. No answer. You re-execute the code and it works  wonderful. Two weeks later, the hang occurs again. You are the victim of a problem  dead end  (deadlock).

A dead end is a concept that is easy to explain and hard to avoid. Imagine that you are walking  sidewalk.  Someone  located  on the  your  way,  So  what  you  deviate  to the left.  Trying  avoid  you, the oncoming passer-by deviates to the right. And you are face to face again. Now you  deviate to the right, he goes to the left ... and so on ad infinitum. Such a situation is called  a dead end.

Output  from  this  embarrassing  provisions  enough  simple  for  of people  -  in  end  ends  who-  it goes the other way. Let's say you are walking to the left and an oncoming pedestrian is walking to the left - and you  disperse. If we could insert a human brain into a computer that would  intermediary in blocking computer situations, we would have a way out. Unfortunately,  state of the art  technology so far  not  reached this level.

But how does this affect Java programming? Replace people on the sidewalk with streams.  Let's say we have two protected resources file1 and file2\. Let's assume that to complete  The task thread needs both resources. The first thread grabs file1 for itself. At the same  most  time  second  flow  captures  file2.  First  flow  now  tries  seize  file2,  but  not

maybe  his  receive,  suspends  his  performance  And  waiting.  Second  flow  tries  seize  file1 and is also waiting. So we have two threads waiting for resources that they never  will be able to receive. Since no thread can get both files needed to complete  work,  they  will  wait indefinitely.  This  classical  happening  dead end.

We can handle deadlock in two ways. As you know, "disease is easier to prevent,  than to treat". We must do everything we can to avoid this situation. We need  design our streams so that we know how they are grabbing contentious resources. Let's  design each thread to hit file1 first. The first thread would grab the file,  and the second thread will wait. The first thread can then get file2, do the necessary  operations and  release  both resources.  IN  this  case decision  simply.

But  some  dead ends  to avoid  much  more difficult.  Sometimes  so  more difficult,  what  better  have  deal with a dead end, trying to find it in various ways. We could start a flow  which would watch other threads; if it seems to him that there is no progress in  task is not present, it tries to identify the problem. Fixing the problem in general  forces one or more threads to yield protected resources. Newly Released  resources may allow other threads to complete the operation and yield resources, which may  unblock the program.

If all this looks complicated, it is only because it is really difficult. If you  going  experiment  from  multiple  resources,  get ready  read  some  textbooks. Let me offer one piece of advice: avoid the need to block  multiple resources. This is where the problems start. The more quantity  resources  required by each thread,  topics  it gets harder  problem.

## Variables  volatile

The final topic of this chapter is the volatile variable modifier, with which most  programmers will not have to face. Let's read the official language definition  Java and then try to understand its meaning: "a variable declared with the volatile modifier,  is known to change asynchronously. The compiler is warned to use such  variables need to be more carefully." To understand the use of the adverb "thoroughly" in this  context, you should have a good understanding of the Java Virtual Machine. What is a volatile variable? Imagine that you have a variable that is real in  memory  missing,  but  actually  her  meaning  changes.  Protozoa  example  -  signal  modem  about the presence of a carrier in the line. This signal is given when you are connected. Since this variable  is changed by an external source, it is treated as volatile. This value may  change between two operations, which could cause errors in some  situations, so we want the compiler to reload the value each time we  we appeal  to a volatile variable.

If you do not use native (native) methods and do not access hardware  registrars  or  others  values  changing  data,  to you,  probably,  never  not  have to  define variables as volatile. ## When  needed  machine dependent  libraries

When writing individual applications, it is desirable to use a DLL. Because C-  extremely popular language, it often turns out that what you are about to do is already  is done with C libraries. Thanks to this, you don't have to rewrite everything in Java -  enough  refer to  DLL.

Applet programmers can also use the DLL, but to a lesser extent than  when writing separate applications. Since the C language is not platform independent,  DLLs cannot be sent over the Internet; otherwise they will sooner or later get on the platform, on  which they cannot be fulfilled. In addition, there are problems when using the DLL,  related to applet security, because C was not created when C was created.  provided  security  security  information  on the  distributed  computers.

However, some Java-enabled Web browsers allow the applet  use any libraries that were previously installed on the client side.  What  this  means  for  programmer  writing  applets?  If  you  doing  in  his  organizations  intranets, you can make sure that the simple C library is installed on  client side, and make sure that it does not contain viruses and that it cannot be  abuse. Then you can let your applets do some things that you don't  wanted  would  let everyone  applets  (for example,  Access to  file system).

If compression software is your favorite toy, you can  distribute a CD containing the DLL or write a program to download this software  software from the Internet. After checking your DLL for viruses, it can be  install so that a Java-enabled Web browser can find it. your library is not  will experience the limitations of the underlying applet model, while at the same time benefiting from  connections to a Java-enabled Web browser. For example, you can use the DLL to  in order to link your spreadsheet program directly to the applet associated with  exchange price server. Or you can make games over the Internet faster due to the fact that  on the client side, graphics will be created, accessible through your DLL. Then you can  use Java networking properties purely for communication, not for downloading weighty  resources.

So, DLLs can be useful for developing Netscape applications. Before moving on to  all the tricks of building a DLL, we need to understand why DLLs are important to the time shell  Java runtime. Java is a platform-independent language, but it still requires some kind of connection with  operating system. This connection is provided by DLLs connected to the API. DLLs play an important role  deciding what parts of a Java program are allowed to do in a given environment.  Because DLLs are not platform independent, they play a key role in porting  Java as a whole to new platforms. Later in this chapter, when examining the questions  creating Java packages, we'll see how building an API makes it easier to port this to  different  shells  time  execution.

Much of the interest in Java is due to the fact that two freely available Web  browsers, Netscape and Hotjava, can download and execute Java applets over the Internet. Applets  very closely connected with the Internet and networks in general. Therefore, it is not at all surprising that the Java API  includes a large package of network classes. Of course, since applets cannot  download data from files on the local computer, they must store data on the network and  bring them back from there. The networking classes contained in the API can be divided into two main  groups: classes dealing with sockets and classes dealing with URLs. # sockets

The idea of a socket is inextricably linked to TCP/IP, the protocol used on the Internet. By  Essentially, a socket is a continuous data connection between two hosts on a network. He  determined by the network address of the endpoint, as well as the port on each  host. Computers on a network direct incoming data streams from the network to special  receiving programs, assigning each program a separate number - the program port.  Similarly, when output is generated, the program initiating the data transfer  the port number for the transaction is assigned. The remote computer cannot respond to input  data. TCP/IP reserves certain port numbers for special protocols -  for example, 25 for SMTP and 80 for HTTP. All port numbers less than 1024 are reserved for  everyone  host for system  administrator.

Java  API  implements  Class  for  implementation  interactions  sockets  -  java.net.Socket.

//  host  unknown

}  catch  (IOException  e)  {

//  mistake  I/O  in  time  connections

}

# Unlinkable  datagrams

The TCP/IP protocol also supports the delivery of non-binding datagrams and their return from  using UDP (User Datagram Packet, "User Datagram Packet"). UDP datagrams  just like TCP sockets, they allow you to communicate with a remote host using the TCP / IP protocol. Unlike  sockets  tcp,  implementing  connection  from  logical  connection,  datagrams  UDP  contact  no logical connection. If a TCP socket can be compared to a phone call, then  A UDP datagram can be compared to a telegram. Delivery of a UDP datagram is not guaranteed, and  even if such a datagram is delivered, there is no guarantee that it was delivered correctly. If you  decide to use datagrams in your program, you will have to deal with lost or  unordered packets.

Because of  unreliability  UDP  majority  programmers  at  writing  network  applications

prefer to work with TCP sockets. However, you may decide to use  datagrams if you want to write a Java client for an existing UDP server like NFS  version 2\. In addition, datagrams have a service  header  (overhead) takes less  places than  on a TCP socket, because when sending or receiving datagrams, no mechanisms are needed  handshaking or flow control. Besides,  UDP datagrams can be used on a Java server that sends a periodically updated  information to clients. If the server, instead of establishing a TCP connection for  each client will just send UDP datagrams, it will do less work and,  respectively,  work  faster.

Two  class  in  Java  associated  from  datagrams  UDP  -  DatagramPacket  And  datagram socket.

# streams

Java  API  for  management  input  And  weekend  data  programs  uses  flows.  Flow

is, in fact, a method of transferring data from a program to some external device, for example  to a file or network. At one end you put something and it comes to the other end (Fig. 13-  one). The main stream classes are InputStream and OutputStream included in the package  java.io. In this section, we will also look at a rich package of advanced stream types,  which greatly simplifies the transfer of data compared to using  bytes directly.

![](Images/image09306.gif)

## Input  streams

#### 
Rice.  13.1.

There are some difficulties when passing input from a remote device.  Majority  input  flows  really  transmitted  across  device,  which  maybe  work  significantly slower than the program using them. Not the best (although the most  simple) the programmer's solution would be to wait for a slow or already finished  data transmission. Network communication speeds vary widely, often with  while passing data, the transmission hangs for a few seconds or minutes. InputStream class  built  so  the way  to  relatively  easily  decrease  similar  delays.

The InputStream class defines a method that returns the number of bytes that can be read from  flow without blocking, that is, for the free time until new data arrives. Methods  stream reads block until at least part of the stream is available.  requested data. This means that if you try to read data that is not yet  appeared, then the thread controlling the data passage will wait until at least part of the data  will come and then continue to work. If the data never arrives, the thread will wait until  until the socket expires. If the end of the data stream is reached, the read method  returns -1\. When an error occurs, all methods throw an IOException. Methods  class InputStream  are given in  tab. 13-5.

Be aware that the DataInputStream methods do not parse the incoming  text to detect characters similar to Java simple types, and the DataOutputStream methods do not  write a textual representation of the variables passing through them. These methods read and  write variables to the stream exactly as they are represented in virtual memory  Java  in car.

For example, when you call readInt, it reads 32 bits from the stream and then returns  an integer corresponding to those 32 bits. It does not parse the string of text data to  find something that looks like an integer. Similarly, the writeInt method of the DataOutputStream  will not write the number "10" to the stream if you pass an integer whose value is not equal to 10\. It  will write a sequence of 32 bits which, when interpreted as an integer, will produce  value 10\. ## Parsing  data  textual  flow

The StreamTokenizer class, similar to the DataInputStream class, is built on top of a regular stream  inputstream. StreamTokenizer differs from other extensions of InputStream types in that it does not  is a direct subclass of the InputStream class - if you use the class  StreamTokenizer, you won't be able to use the normal InputStream methods on it. But  Stream Tokenizer will allow you to read some simple Java data types, namely strings  and double-precision floating-point numbers, from the text data stream. You will need  this  property  for  connections  from  server,  transmitting  data  in  textual  form,  for example  MUD.

Class  StreamTokenizer  shares  flow  inputstream  on the  pieces,  called  tokens  (tokens).

This  Class  distinguishes  five  species  tokens:  words,  numbers,  symbols  EOL,  symbols  EOF,  ordinary  symbols.  Let be,  e.g. stream  contains  the following data:

You  are  user  nine  of  one hundred:

StreamTokenizer  will return  from  this  flow  seven  tokens.  "you",  "are",  "user"  And  "of"  will

will be treated as strings, "9" and "100" will be treated as numbers, and ":" will be returned as  normal character.

The working method of the StreamTokenizer class is the nextToken method. He reads the next  token from the stream and returns an integer indicating what type of token it found. If the token  is a word, number, EOL or EOF, respectively the integer will be TT_WORD, TT_NUMBER,  TT_EOL or TT_EOF. These TT_* variables are defined as static integers in the class  StreamTokenizer. If the token is a regular character, the method returns the value of that  symbol. If the token type is TT_WORD, the actual string is placed in the sval variable  class  StreamTokenizer.  If  type  token  is an  TT_NUMBER,  real  meaning  type  double  placed  in  variable nval  class  Stream Tokenizer,  owned  to  this  type.

By default, the StreamTokenizer class understands numbers as a sequence of digits,  maybe,  divided  dot,  ending  from  each  sides  space  or  ordinary  symbol. He understands words in two ways - as a sequence of letters of the alphabet,  ending on each side with a space or a regular character, or as something  containing single  or  double quotes.

There are many ways to use the StreamTokenizer class. You can set a new  a set of characters recognized as word characters, as whitespace characters, or as regular characters  symbols. You can set the StreamTokenizer class to ignore comments.  You can set a single character as a comment character, and each time as a StreamTokenizer  will read that character, it will ignore it and everything following it to the nearest  EOL symbol. This class can also understand comments like /*...*/ and // ... You can even  set new line separator characters. Let's consider a simple example. Let's say your input  information is as follows  way:

#This  a comment  This  Group  words?

:This  whole  line!!!:

By default Stream Tokenizer will understand "#", "?" And "!" like ordinary characters, but all  the rest is like words. Let's say we created a StreamTokenizer and modified it with the following  way:

InputStream in = mySocket.getInputStream();  StreamTokenizer st = new StreamTokenizer(in);  st.commentChar('#');

st.wordChar('?','?');  st.quoteChar(':');

Now StreamTokenizer will completely ignore the first line, return "words?" as a whole  word and assume that everything between the colons in the third line is a string.  For  the best  acquaintance  from  methods  class  StreamTokenizer  consider  tab.  13-10.

## Interaction  InterApplet  c  channels

Java  API  implements  connection  flows  data  between  various  streams  (threads).  This  property  can be used to, without creating a rigid and complex system of methods, to give  the ability for threads to communicate. You can create a pair of piped data streams,  PipedInputStream and PipedOutputStream. Anything that will be written to the PipedOutputStream will be  received on its connected PipedInputStream. One thread can build a pair of channel  data streams and give one of them to another stream. Now threads can communicate in one  direction through the data stream. If you need to communicate in two directions, you can create  another  couple  channels and  ask  streams  opposite types.

This  method  useful  not  only  for  inter-stream  connections  in  one  applet,  but  is he  also  allows

applets share context (for example, on a Web page) in order to communicate with each other.  The AppleContext applet provides a getApplets method that lists the applets it  provides  their  resources,  And  method  getApplet,  which the  beret  name  applet  And  returns  link  on the  named  applet,  if  such  exists.  Names  applets  are given  in  HTML document:

<APPLET  CODE="..."  WIDTH=###  HEIGHT=###  NAME="...">

By making a link to the applet you want to chat with, you can pair  channel data streams and pass one of them to this applet using some  predefined method. This can be done in many ways. For simplicity, we  decided to create a subclass of the Applet class, ListenApplet (listening applet), acting in  as a passive listener. Another applet can request an OutputStream from it, write  there the data and tell it to read the data from the stream. ListenApplet takes data from the stream,  interprets  them  how  text  And  prints  in  TextArea.  Here  program  for  ListenApplet.

## Compound  from  help  class  URLConnection

If you are using a URL that requires some additional input information,  for example a URL to a CGI script, or if you need more information about a certain resource, you  you can use the openConnection method. This method returns a URLConnection object,  associated with the URL. The URLConnection class contained in the Java API gives an abstract  representing the actual connection between the computer hosting the applet and  computer,  containing  this resource.

You may want to use a CGI script as a simple  in-server support for your Java applet. Applets cannot simply write  files to your client or your server, but you can easily write a secure script, and  this will give you read or write access to the files on the server. Then Java-  applets will be able to link the URL to your script, allowing you to send  data to a network share so that your applet can pass its file requests to the script  across  CGI variables.  This  scenario  maybe,  in  my  turn,  fulfill  necessary  operations  with files and report the status of the operation performed in the output. This technique  used  in  Chapter 17 , "Interacting with CGI: The Java Store."

Some protocols, in addition to allowing access to network resources, may issue  information about the resource, such as the MIME type or the date the resource was last modified.  Class  URLConnection  contains  sufficient  kit  methods  for  access  to  this  data.

A URLConnection can be created using the openConnection method of the URL class, or using  the desired URL as an argument. The URLConnection class gives programmers more  information and better management of the resource identified by the URL. According to the Java API description,  this class is abstract; subclasses implemented for specific protocols,  included in the JDK. This applies to HTTP, FILE and DOC protocols (FILE URL is used for  local files, and the DOC URL is used in the Hotjava browser). Netscape Navigator 2.0  allows  applets  at  work  from  URL  use only  HTTP protocol.

GET /index.html HTTP/1.0  HTTP/1.0  200  document  follows

Server: NCSA/1.4  content-type:  text/html

Last modified:  Fri,  08  Mar  1996  20:24:18

content length:  4611

<html>

If  we  create  URLConnection  for  pages  index.html  from  given  example,  method  getContentType will return "text/html" and the getContentLength method will return "4611". notice, that  determining these values using HTTP is extremely easy - the server returns them in  header  HTTP.  Many  other  protocols are not  give  this  information.

Now let's return to the working tool of the methods of the URLConnection class, to the getContent method.  Exactly  this  method  really  starts,  when  we  call  method  getContent  on the  URL.  For  start  the getContent method attempts to determine the content type of the resource in question by examining either  HTTP header, either the stream itself, or the filename extension. Deciding which MIME type  use, the getContent method queries the ContentHandler class for the given MIME type, and  passed to the ContentHandler class.

## Types  MIME  And  Class  ContentHandler

Each MIME type can have its own ContentHandler class. This ContentHandler class in  ultimately processes the resource data when we call getContent on a URL or  URLConnection. The ContentHandler class consists of a single getContent method that uses  URLConnection  how  argument  And  returns  an object,  on  opportunities  related to  resource.

For example, a resource with a MIME type of "image/gif" would most likely be returned as an Image or some  then subclass Image from the getContent method. ContentHandler class as per Java API descriptions  is abstract; subclasses of the ContentHandler class give implementations for various types  mime.  Below  given not  very complicated  ContentHandler  for  any  types  "text/*":

import  java.net.*;  import  java.io.*;

public  class  TextContentHandler  extends  ContentHandler  {  public  Object  getContent(URLConnection  urlc)  {

try  {

inputstream  is;

is  =  urlc.getInputStream();

DataInputStream  ds;

ds  =  new  DataInputStream(is);  int  length;

length  =  urlc.getContentLength();  if  (length!=-1)  {

byte  b[]  =  new  byte[length];  ds.readFully(b);

String  s  =  new  string(b,0);

}  else  {

//  length  unknown

String  s  =  "";

int i = is.read();  while  (i!=-1)  {

s = s+(char)i;  i  =  is.read();

}

}

return  s;

}  catch  (Exception  e)  {

e.printStackTrace();  return  null;

}

}

}

How does the URLConnection choose the appropriate ContentHandler when calling getContent? at first  the MIME type of the stream is selected and the ContentHandler for that MIME type is queried from  ContentHandlerFactory. According to Java API descriptions, ContentHandler Factory is an interface. He  consists of a single createContentHandler method that uses a string variable in  as an argument and returns a ContentHandler. The string value specifies which type  MIME the given ContentHandler can use. Below is the text of the program for a simple  ContentHandlerFactory,  which the  maybe  used  our  TextContentHandler:

import  java.net.*;  import  java.io.*;

public  class  MyContentHandlerFactory  extends  Object

implements ContentHandlerFactory {  public ContentHandler  createContentHandler(String  type)  {

if  (type.startsWith("text"))  {

return  new  TextContentHandler();

}

else  {

}

}

}

return  null;

## Definition  interactions  client-server

When synchronous updating of information is required, coordination is an important task.  server with multiple clients. For example, if you want to update all  clients connected to the server, passing them some special data or commands, you  should make their server error tolerant so that it doesn't hang when trying to  hand over  network data.

In our communication program, it is necessary that all clients receive data from the server  at the same time, so that multiple strings submitted by the same user are together when  other users will see them. We will do this with just one independent thread,  working with output data to clients. In this case, an independent thread can freely  send data to all connected clients without being bound to input from any  then a certain input. Since we are only doing one operation per thread, namely  write down  data  clients,  we  Can  to be  sure,  what  customer  will receive  data  in  then  same  most  time. In order to better coordinate such interaction, we must consider the issues  related  with time,  complexity  And  server speed.

### Distribution  time

We have already talked about the need to write data to client ports at the same time. Although in  this is not possible in full, our task is to reduce the time required to write data  everyone  clients,  So  to  at  them  created  impression,  what  data  transmitted  simultaneously.  The free-running stream we use to write data  connected clients can be given higher priority than streams  reading data from each client. We can wait until the writing stream  will finish and then start reading data from connected clients. Another temporary  aspect,  which the  necessary  have  in  mind  tied  from  forwarding  data  from  client  on the  server.

If  two  client  send  data  on the  server  simultaneously,  flow,  recording  weekend  data may be busy. To avoid crossing, you need to use  synchronized block  programs,  what  explained  in  section  below.

### Structure  connections

The fact that we have several connections brings our communication server to a more  difficult level than it seems at first. We need to watch out for a few things  first of all - for the state of each connection. If the user interrupts the communication client without  having notified the server about this, we will receive a delayed connection, which will  function incorrectly. The writer thread may attempt to write to  non-existent connection, and we will keep trying to read data from the server  this connection. The solution to this problem is twofold: when an operation is performed with an already  broken connection - throw an exception and terminate the connection; in addition, perform  preventive cleaning of connections, periodically checking them. Such check and exception  links free up valuable system resources. In our example, prophylactic  connection checking is performed by the ConnectionWatcher class. It also runs in its own  flow, so that he can perform his duties without delaying the execution of the rest  functions.

We need to be able to read from the attached client without losing  ability to read from other links. If we use a loop that simply does  sequentially readln on each connected client, we may end up with the fact that  we will wait for the user who no longer works with the communication client, but left him  running and went to dinner. To solve this problem, you need to make the entire server  asynchronous - that is, create a reading thread for each connection. At the same time, individual  the thread can wait as long as necessary for the user to enter a message without  suspending the server. When the user enters a message, we simply pass it to  entry  (then  eat  on the  his  own  flow),  And  message  will  recorded  to each  client.

The reader thread can immediately resume reading another message sent  user. Due to the fact that each connection has its own reading thread, we  no need to wait for each individual link to finish reading data, and thus  the server turns out really asynchronous. However, care must be taken to  do not refer to the split writer stream and ConnectionWatcher when trying to  use  another  flow.  For  this  in  block  programs,  to  who can  to attempt

implement  multiple  access,  made  synchronous  descriptions.

As mentioned above, the ServerWrite thread writes output to all links. For that  to "wake up" the ServerWriter, a notify call is used. When ServerWriter  resumes execution, it examines the predefined variables for the presence of  data to be sent to connected clients. To keep the weekend  data and avoid intersection in case two reading threads make a push call,  The first in, first out (FIFO) data structure is used. FIFO class in detail  considered  in  chapter  17 , "Interaction with CGI:  Java Store".

If we were to parse input and output data, we would need  an additional thread whose task would be to process requests from other threads, their  analysis  And  forwarding  data.  This  increases  complexity,  because  what  US  maybe  would need  such an additional stream for each connection. In our communication server, we do not perform  analysis  data.

### Speed  work

Since we have to create a thread for each connection, the number of threads given  server can be quite large. In a situation where many threads are fighting for two  constantly present thread ServerWriter and ConnectionWatcher, the question arises of whether  how fast the server is. This cannot be ignored if we expect the presence  a large number of connections. We should, as far as possible, simplify our two classes with  considering their active use. In addition, if a large number of customers are expected  communication, we might want to double the server itself to share the load. Then we  you have to deal with multiple servers and data passing through them, which is  coming out  beyond the scope of this chapter.

To improve the structure and performance of the server, we will widely use  multithreading property. We will create a separate thread for each connected client and  start three other threads: a ServerWriter thread that writes data to each  attached  customer;  base  flow  chatserver,  listening,  when  new  clients  trying  establish a connection with the server; and a ConnectionWatcher thread that cleans up broken connections. Like us  discussed in the Relationship Structure section, we may need more additional threads,  so don't be afraid to use them! Threads make it easy to manage  data flows and perform complex interaction, which will be seen when considering  program text. True, streams add additional headers to the entire system  messages (overhead), but, as a rule, while the number of connections is not very large, the flows are  spent resources.

Note that there are a lot of try and catch statements in the communication server program. To  the program was more resistant to errors, it is important to fully exploit the possibilities  exception handling. For example, when starting the ping process, we execute  exception handling. In a more complex server, exceptions play a very important role for  stabilization  general  functions.  Treatment  exceptions  should  produced  even  in  volume  case,  when there is a low probability of an error occurring. In addition, exceptions may  be used to call methods for cleaning up, freeing system resources, debugging, and  tight control over the passage  flow  data  server.

# Building  client  communication

The communication client applet is contained in a Web browser window (Figure 15-2). This applet  automatically connects to port 6001 on the host from which the web page is loaded.  We open a frame so that the user can enter their name and introduce themselves to others  users; create two independent streams - one for reading from the network and the second for writing to  net. As a result, our client is truly asynchronous, since the user  can type his own message while new messages from others appear on the screen  users.

package ventana.awt;  import  java.awt.*;  import  java.awt.image.*;  import  java.util.*;

public class BufferedImageGraphics {  private  Graphics  graphicsBuf;  private  Image  imageBuf;

//  use  for  fulfillment  double  buffering

private ImageObserver imageObsv;  private  Vector  curImages=new  Vector();  private  int  originalWidth;

private  int  originalHeight;

private  Rectangle  cropRect=new  Rectangular();

//  region  pruning

private  boolean  waitToTouchImages=false;

//  guards  buffer  in  time  process

//  additions  or  removal  images

color  backgroundColor;

public  BufferedImageGraphics(ImageObserver  observer,  color  c)  {  imageObsv=observer;

backgroundColor=c;

}

public  boolean  needBuffer()  {

return  (graphicsBuf==null  &&  imageBuf==null);}  public  void  setBuffer(Image  i)  {

imageBuf=i;  originalWidth=i.getWidth(imageObsv);  originalHeight=i.getHeight(imageObsv);  graphicsBuf=imageBuf.getGraphics();  graphicsBuf.setColor(backgroundColor);

graphicsBuf.fillRect(0,0,originalWidth,originalHeight);}  public  synchronized  void  addImage(PositionedImage  pi)  {

while  (waitToTouchImages);  waitToTouchImages=true;

// Since we have to draw the picture and remove the crop, maybe  arise

//  command  reset  buffer  before  graduation  work.  This  will lead  to  chaos.  Rectangle  r=pi.getRect();

//  find out  how  this  affects  on the  region  pruning

if  (cropRect==null  ||  cropRect.isEmpty())  cropRect=r;  else

cropRect=cropRect.union(r);  curImages.addElement(pi);

if  (graphicsBuf!=null)

graphicsBuf.drawImage  (pI.getImage(),rx,ry,backgroundColor,imageObsv);

waitToTouchImages=false;}

private  PositionedImage  getCurPosImage(int  i)  {

return (PositionedImage)curImages.elementAt(i);}  public  synchronized  boolean  removeImage(PositionedImage  I)

{

while  (waitToTouchImages);  waitToTouchImages=true;

int  imgIndx=curImages.indexOf(I);  if (imgIndx==-1) {  waitToTouchImages=false;

return  false;}

Rectangle  clearReg=getCurPosImage(imgIndx).getRect();

//  region  for  cleaning

curImages.removeElementAt(imgIndx);

graphicsBuf.fillRect  (clearReg.x,clearReg.y,clearReg.width,clearReg.height);

//  cleaning  areas

cropRect=new  Rectangular();

//  preparation  to  reset  areas  pruning

for (int i=0;i<curImages.size();i++) {  PositionedImage  somePI=getCurPosImage(i);  Image  img=somePI.getImage();

Rectangle  someRect=somePI.getRect();  cropRect.add(someRect);

int  x=someRect.x;  int  y=someRect.y;

graphicsBuf.drawImage(img,x,y,imageObsv);

}

waitToTouchImages=false;  return  true;}

public  Graphics  graphicsContext(Rectangle  r)  {  cropRect.add(r);

return  graphicsBuf.create(rx,ry,r.width,r.height);}  public  synchronized  void  paintBuffer(Graphics  g)  {

while(waitToTouchImages);  waitToTouchImages=true;  Rectangle  curCR=g.getClipRect();  if  (curCR==null)  curCR=new

Rectangle(0,0,originalWidth,originalHeight);  g.clipRect(cropRect.x,cropRect.y,cropRect.width,cropRect.height);  g.drawImage(imageBuf,0,0,backgroundColor,imageObsv);  g.clipRect(0,0,originalWidth,originalHeight);

cropRect=new  Rectangular();

//  reset  areas  pruning

waitToTouchImages=false;

}

}

## Creation  analyzer

Before we start working with the applet, we need to create a parser. As we spoke at  when writing the Configuration class, the task of the analyzer is to check the correctness  configuration file and pass information to the Configuration object. Besides,  the parser must interpret the exceptions that the Configuration object may throw,  And  create  understandable messages.

Thanks to  structure  our  language  analyzer  must  view  document  only  one  once.

The main thing that is required here is the translation of tags into variables that can be passed  object  configuration.  except  Togo,  US  necessary  several  routines,  which  will  extradite  more user friendly messages than exception messages. Best  a way to make messages understandable is to follow the line number. As we said before  US  still need comments and empty lines:

package ventana.aia;  import java.util.*;  import java.net.*;  import java.io.*;  import  ventana.util.*;

public  class  AIAnimParser  extends  ConfFileParser  {  private  DataInputStream  conf;

private  int  lineNumber=1;

private  Stack  tokenStack=new  stack();

private  final  String  packageName="ventana.aia.";  private final String beginClassToken="<";  private  final  String  endClassToken=">";

private  final  String  classNameDescript="type";  private final String closureToken="</";  private  final  String  assignString="=";

private  final  String  commentChar="#";  int  hierarchyDepth=0;

final  String  validClasses[]={"ActionAnimApplet","ActionImageCanvas",  "ActionImageAnimation","ActionImage","ActionArea"};

public  AIAnimParser(URL  U)  throws  IOException{  conf=new DataInputStream(U.openStream());}  public  boolean  start()  {

try  {

while(conf.available()>0) {  String  curLine=conf.readLine();  if  (!parseLine(curLine))  {

messageError("Parsing  stopped");  return  false;}

lineNumber++;}

}  catch(IOException  e)  {

messageError("Error  reading  configuration  file",e);

}

return  true;

}

public  boolean  parseLine(String  line)  {  line=line.trim();

//  carved  empty  a place

if  (line.startsWith(commentChar)  ||  line.length()==0)

return  true;

if  (line.startsWith(closureToken))

{return  closeCurrentToken(line);

}

if  (line.startsWith(beginClassToken))

{return  parseToken(line);

}

//  transfer  param/value

// current object  passParam(line);  return  true;

//  If  value  not  recognized,  not  stop  analysis.

//  Call  for  completion  configuration  on the  closureToken  will cause  errors.

}

public  void  passParam(String  line)  {

StringTokenizer  splitter=new  StringTokenizer(line,assignString);  String  param=splitter.nextToken();

String  value=splitter.nextToken();

try  {

configureObject.passToCurrent(param,value);}

catch  (ConfigurationInvalidParameterException  e)  {  messageError("invalid  parameter",e,curClass());

}

catch  (ConfigurationInvalidValueException  e)

{messageError("invalid  value",e,curClass());}

}

public boolean parseToken(String token) {  int  start=beginClassToken.length();

int  end=token.length()-  endClassToken.length();  token=token.substring(start,end);

StringTokenizer  splitter=new  StringTokenizer(token,"=");  String  baseClassName=splitter.nextToken();

String  subClassName=splitter.nextToken();  if (subClassName==null) {  subClassName=baseClassName;}

if (baseClassName==null){  messageError("No  class  specified");  return  false;}

else  return  configureNewClass(baseClassName,subClassName);

}

# What  you  learn  from  this  chapters

In this chapter, we will create a "Java Store" applet, a "shopping cart" program that  will allow visitors to the virtual store to view and select products. Here are some  questions,  which we will be discussing:

*   Usage  HTTP  for  receiving  data  for  applet.

The complete source code for the classes discussed in this chapter is included on the CD-ROM,  attached to the book. This disk can be used by those readers who work with Windows  95/NT  or  Macintosh  users  UNIX  should  address  to  web page  online  Companion,  which contains the accompanying materials for this book (address [http://www.vmedia.com/](http://www.vmedia.com/)  java.html).

# the contract

Imagine that your customer wants to improve an interactive bookstore. IN  this store uses eye-catching graphics, the latest HTML techniques and  a "shopping cart" system into which customers can select purchased books.  Shopping cart system keeps track of what the user has selected while browsing  online store catalog. While browsing the directory, the user can click a button,  to  add  product  to  his  list  acquired  goods.  Existing  system  carts  for shopping is implemented as a series of CGI scripts that produce HTML forms from  interactive catalog and process the selection of goods for purchase. However, the state  serving this  shop,  complains  on the  the following  HTML forms restrictions:

*   No real user interaction. The user can only  click a button to add or remove an item from the shopping cart, what is wrong  conveniently,  how  wanted  would.
*   The web server is heavily loaded with constant requests that the program issues  carts  for  shopping,  insofar as  user  looks through  lots of  goods.  Each  an action performed by the user (for example, choosing a product for purchase),  must  call  program  CGI  on the  Web server  which,  in  my  turn,  should  track  to save  previous  choice.
*   Changing the Web page of an online store is a time consuming task. Appearance  new products and moving products from one page to another require adding  and changes in many connections; as the store grows, these connections become more and more complicated -  And  at  personnel already  not  enough  time  on his  service.

The growth of the online store is a prerequisite for our customer, so  current restrictions should be lifted. We provide a Java applet that can  these problems. It will work with an existing online store, so  the transition from an HTML-based store to a Java-based store will be smooth.  Users whose Web browsers are not capable of running Java applets will still be able to  receive  access  to  goods  companies.  Origin  orders,  destined  existing  an online store or a new store based on Java will be indifferent to the state,  which the  handles  orders,  So  what  no  additional  learning  not  would need.

# Properties

The Java applet will allow the user to manage the store using a menu. Each item  the menu will represent the new department of the store. Nested menus will allow the state  organize the store into subdivisions. For example, in the "Programming" department, it is possible  subsections "Java Books", "C++ Books" and "Visual Basic Books". The Java store will have  "basket  for  shopping."  IN  addition  to  list  containing  current  choice  user,  this  program  will allow  user to delete products  from  list  acquisitions.

IN  Java store  will  And  reference  menu,  to  user  could,  to  example,  send  letter  with a question to the store owner or to receive detailed ordered information.  The java store will consist of two main panels: the left panel will contain  product image  in current  departments  shop,  but  right  -  detailed  description  goods,  which the  selected  on the  left panel.

After selecting a product, the user can click on the "Check out of Store" button, by which this  acquisition  will  contributed  in  list  And  sent  scenario  CGI  on the  web server.  This  information  can be packaged to be identical to currently existing interactive  data,  based  on the  HTML forms.  This  will allow  US  call  that  same  most  CGI program.

internal  device  Java Store  is an  more  complicated  how  aforementioned  external  user interface. Menus are organized dynamically - they are formed based on  files permanently located on the Web server. This allows you to set up a Java store without  any programming. The store staff can replace the products offered, they  descriptions and organization of departments by modifying plain text files. java store reads these  files  And  forms an interface  user  according to their  instructions.

The screen will display a large panel containing images  products in the current departments of the store, a panel in which you can show the description of the product, and  a panel for a list of selected products (that is, a shopping cart). ## Class  FIFO

The FIFO class is an extension of the Vector class available in the API. Vector is a class  expandable array in the java.util package. We add some methods to match  FIFO data structure. FIFO is used in the formation of the user interface, which  makes it much easier to keep track of the data of this interface. We can put objects in the FIFO in  special order and get them back in the same order using the appropriate  push and pop methods. We also have an isEmpty method which checks if the list is  empty:

## Reading  data  about  configuration  And  initialization

Class  Store  -  the foundation  applet.  He  causes  Class  StoreWindow,  which the  is an  frame  outside  web browser. The store is called from a Web page with an <APPLET> tag. The main purpose of the class  Store is to receive and parse Java store configuration files for  their use by the StoreWindow class. We select idx files starting with the Store.idx file and  then  recursively  receiving  rest  required  idx files  from  specified  subdirectories:

Also, we will pass "Store.idx" as the default  name  index file:

We  getting started  from  methods  URL  applet,  getDocumentBase.getHost  And  getDocumentBase.getPort,  to use the HTTPget class to get the index file from the web server. An object  Index HTTPget now allows us to get to the idx file using the Results method. httpget  called repeatedly  for  various  idx files,  till  all  they  not  will  received.

Then, using StringTokenizer, we split the received idx files into parts by characters  newline \n, since when structuring idx files, we placed the data in separate  lines. Now the idx file can contain one of four elements: a menu or a submenu  (then we would have to get another idx-file), or the name of the gif-file, the name of the description file  or identifier. We know the order of the elements, so we must look for the trailing "/",  to define a menu or submenu. If it's a menu or submenu, we call ParseIndex with  path of the directory, which is just the current token, and add the label we  get from the next line in the idx file, delimiting them with the "Menu:" mark. We are adding  all  this  to  our  string  variable  tree  And  transfer  StoreWindow,  which the  then  analyzes  this preformatted list to form the user interface.  The recursive call to ParseIndex parses these menus using the same methods  ParseIndex but with different parameters. This use of recursion prevents us from  need  execution of nested loops  from  introduction  control  points.

If the token is not a catalog (that is, a menu), then it represents a product. We bet  mark,  identifying  element,  added  to  tree,  -  GIF:,  "TXT:"  And  "NAME:".  We  we will  add these three parts for each product, and tags will allow us to debug problems with idx-  files or the formation of the list Tree. We loop inside each idx file until  its processing will not be completed, but we branch several times when recursively  processing menus and submenus. The resulting variable, the string Tree, might look like  confusing, but we use a similar recursive method on the StoreWindow to form  user interface, and this method is very convenient to work with a non-linear form  tree configuration we have here  created.

When the configuration files are parsed and put into a formatted Tree list,  we create a new StoreWindow (getDocumentBase, Tree) to which we pass the current  tree variable configuration. We also pass in the base URL so that we can  use it to get GIF image files and description files from a Web server for  relevant goods.

private  Menu  BuildUI(String  tree)  {  FIFO  PanelAdd  =  new  FIFO();

private  void  ParseTree(StringTokenizer  tree branch,  Menu  menuin,  String  PreviousToken,  FIFO  PanelAdd)

{

StringTokenizer  Leaf;  Menu  subMenu;

String  next;

//  ImagePanel  MenuPanel;

while  (TreeBranch.hasMoreTokens())  {

Leaf  =  new  StringTokenizer(TreeBranch.nextToken(),  ":");  next  =  Leaf.nextToken();

//  are looking for  "Menu"  And  add  new  element  in  menu

if  (!PreviousToken.equals(""))  {

if (next.equalsIgnoreCase("Menu")) {  subMenu  =  new  Menu(PreviousToken);

MenuIn.add(subMenu);

//  recursive  treatment  this  new  submenu

PreviousToken="";  MenuIn=subMenu;

}

else  {

}

}

MenuIn.add(PreviousToken);  PanelAdd.push(PreviousToken);

//  are looking for  "Menu"  And  add  new  element  in  menu

if  (next.equalsIgnoreCase("Menu"))  {

ParseTree(TreeBranch,  menuin,  Leaf.nextToken(),  panelAdd);

}

else if (next.equalsIgnoreCase("GIF")) {  PanelAdd.push(Leaf.nextToken());  ParseTree(TreeBranch,  menuin,  "",  panelAdd);

}

else if (next.equalsIgnoreCase("TXT")) {  PanelAdd.push(Leaf.nextToken());  ParseTree(TreeBranch,  menuin,  "",  panelAdd);

}

else if (next.equalsIgnoreCase("NAME")) {  PanelAdd.push(Leaf.nextToken());  ParseTree(TreeBranch,  menuin,  "",  panelAdd);

}

else  if  (next.equalsIgnoreCase("END"))  {  if  (!PanelAdd.empty())

{

String  panelname  =(String)PanelAdd.pop();  Leaf.nextToken();

<%-2>ProductPicPanel.add(PanelName,  new

ImagePanel(BaseURL,  PanelAdd,  PanelName));<%0>

}

}

}

The BuildUI method actually initializes the ParseTree method. We create a new object  FIFO, new menu. We then use the StringTokenizer with the Tree, separating the tokens by new character.  lines.  tree  we  created  in  classroom  Store  from  data  configuration,  received  from  web servers.

It  It was  previously  formatted  And  orderly  So,  to  recursive  method  ParseTree could use it. Most of the work in the BuildUI method is  correct  using recursion  with method  ParseTree.

As we said, the ParseTree method works recursively. It is called when we  facing the new menu. This allows us to handle nested menus without  using nested loops. We call ParseTree with the following parameters:  StringTokenizer containing the tree to be processed; parent menu;  a string containing the previous token; and a FIFO list containing the data for the ImagePanel,  which must be formed with this configuration data. parent menu and  the previous token is required for the submenus. In general, we follow this path in the ParseTree method:  we process the current sheet and get the next sheet, which is a label for  previous one, then we call ParseTree with the rest of the tree. We stop parsing  tree, reaching its end marked "END". During the tree pass, we place  elements to the FIFO PanelAdd buffer. This FIFO is passed to the ImagePanel, which uses  data  in FIFO,  to select an image and product description.

## Interaction  from  asynchronous  server

Chapter 13 , you learned how to use sockets to establish a connection between an applet and  server. However, we haven't touched on the asynchronous connection mode yet. simple server,  for example Finger, serves synchronous data streams - it always waits for a command input and  only then transmits the data. Some servers are asynchronous - they can  send data at any convenient time. These include our chess  server. This means that if one user sends data to the server for another  user,  data  will  transferred  this  user  without  any  warnings.

We  decided  develop  special  receiver  data,  working  in  separate  stream.

Thanks to this, we will be sure that, no matter how busy the applet is at the current moment,  data coming from the network will be accepted. The data receiver reads the data in the form  values of type String received from the InputStream, separating strings as they occur  characters  EOL  or  EOF.  Let's  describe  interface  listener,  allowing  this  do:

package  ventana.io

public  interface  Listener  {

public  void  receiveInput(InputStreamHandler  i,  Object  o);

}

This  method  allows  receiver  data  -  class  InputStreamHandler  -  transfer  values  String read from the InputStream to another object using the method  receiveInput. Listener is capable of accepting any object, but in this case we will  transfer  through him  only  String values.  except  Togo,  we  return link  on the

InputStreamHandler.  She  come in handy  if  US  need  use  And  making a difference  multiple threads at the same time

InputStreamHandler:

package  ventana.io  import  java.io.*;

public  class  InputStreamHandler  implements  runnable  {<Com  private  Thread  engine;

private  DataInputStream  in;  private  Listener  client;

public  InputStreamHandler(InputStream  in,  Listener  client)  {

this.in  =  new  DataInputStream(in);  this.client  =  client;

engine  =  new  thread(this);  engine.start();

}

public  void  close()  {

if  (in!=null)  {

try {in.close();}  catch(IOException  e)  {}

}

engine.stop();

}

public  void  run()  {

if (in == null) {return;}  String  s;

try {s = in.readLine();}  catch  (IOException  e)  {

return;

}}

while  (s  !=  null  &&  engine.isAlive())  {  client.receiveInput(this,s);  try  {s  =  in.readLine();}

catch  (IOException  e)  {s  =  null;}

}

}

}

When an InputStreamHandler object is constructed, it creates a DataInputStream based on  of the InputStream object passed to it and starts the stream. The run method reads lines from  DataInputStream  And  transmits  them  client  Listener  from  help  method  receiveInput.  If  going on  an exception  IOException,  InputStreamHandler  simply  stops  reading  data.

## Creation  chess  boards

The code that forms the chessboard has nothing to do with the code that interacts with  server. Therefore, the board we create can equally well serve both for playing  chess, and, for example, checkers. Our board is quite simple - it consists of 8 squares on  8,  contains several  images  And  responds to  moving  And  clicks  mouse.

Our checkerboard is an extension of the Canvas class, which in turn  is a more or less workable implementation of the abstract Component class. We  decided  not  use  for  boards  Class  Container  on  two  reasons.  Firstly,  Images  chess pieces do not belong to the Component class and therefore cannot be directly  be added to the Container object. Second, a modern implementation of the Java API for Microsoft  Windows does not work correctly if the Container object contains a large  number  objects  Component.

Class  Chess Board  bears  responsibility  behind  drawing  chess  boards  And  generation  moves.

## Connection  chess  boards  from  CIS

We will develop  applet,  which the  uses  for  implementation  CIS client  how  our  chess  board, and the receiver of asynchronous data. Below is the text of the program,  parsing the CIS output and issuing a CIS command. If we design well  our  applet,  this  will  the only one  chapter,  containing  specific  for  CIS  program.

The checkerboard should not be placed in the applet itself, because CIS allows several  users to observe and even participate in multiple games at the same time. Our client  should not limit the possibilities of CIS, but should, on the contrary, expand them. CIS is watching  games by numbers, and when he sends a message with an updated board, in this message  part number included. Our main applet is designed to contain a set of  chessboards with indexes by game numbers. Each board corresponds to one batch and  located  in own  frame.

### Installation  stopwatch

Instead of  Togo  to  simply  show,  How many  left  time  let's use  the ability of the Java language to work with streams and make the clock count seconds  for the currently active player. The Label class gives a generic non-editable field to the output  text.  Let's expand it  in  Class  stop watch  (stopwatch),  to  receive  label,  which  shows the current time and decrements the variable containing the value every second  time.  General  methods  class StopWatch  are given  in table.  18-2.

table  18-2.  General  methods  class  stop watch

#### Method Description

set(int)  Sets  And  shows  remaining  time.  start()  Starts  Countdown  time.

stop()  Stops timing.  clear()  Fully  stops  clock.

Let's bring  program  for  stopwatch:

import  java.awt.*;

public  class  stop watch  extends  label  implements  runnable  {  private  Thread  engine;

private int time=0;  public  stopwatch()  {

super();

engine  =  new  thread(this);  engine setPriority(3);

}

public  StopWatch(int  i)  {

this();

set(i);

}

The set method sets the time remaining on the stopwatch. He must be  synchronized because different pairs of players may try to set the clock  simultaneously.  If  time  not  negative  reinstall  day off  label,  to  show  time:

public synchronized void set(int i) {  time  =  one;

if  (time>0)  {

int min = time/60;  int sec = time%60;  if  (sec>9)  {

setText(""+min+":"+sec);

}  else  {

setText(""+min+":0"+sec);

}

}  else  {

setText("0:00");

}

}

public  void  start()  {

if  (engine!=null)  {

if  (!engine.isAlive())  {

engine.start();

}  else  {

engine.resume();

}

}

}

public  void  stop()  {

if  (engine!=null)  {

engine.suspend();

}

}

public  void  clear()  {

if  (engine!=null)  {

engine.stop();  engine  =  null;

}

}

public  void  run()  {

while  (engine!=null  &&  engine.isAlive())  {  set(time-1);

try  {

engine sleep(1000);

}  catch  (InterruptedException  e)  {}

}

}

}

ChessFrame is primarily responsible for parsing update messages  playing field and displaying relevant information. Default update message  It was  given  above  on the  rice.  18-1.  CIS  gives  possibility  select  from  existing  set  styles  game boards. The style we have chosen at number 12 sends an update message to  form  one  line,  containing  several  fields,  divided  spaces:

<12>  rnbqkbnr  pppppppp  ----  -----  ----  ----  PPPPPPPP  RNBQKBNR  W  -one  one  one  one  one  0  one  donald  donald  2  0  0  39  39  0  0  one  none  (0:00)

none  0

The first field indicates that the line contains a message about updating the game board in  format 12\. The parent ChessFrame will use this field to determine  the need to call the updateGame method. The next eight fields contain information about  current  able  boards.  Each  figure  corresponds  certain  letter;  white  are celebrated  capital letters and black letters in lowercase. Hyphens denote cells that do not contain  no figures. We will discuss the remaining fields later, as we consider the text of the method.  updateGame.

Here  original  text  class  ChessFrame:

import ChessBoard;  import ChessClient;  import PackerLayout;  import java.awt.*;  import java.util.*;  import  ventana.awt.*;

public  class  ChessFrame  extends  frame  {  private Chess Board;  private ChessClient parent;  private  String  user;
