Frame  contains  two  major  component:  myself  Chess Board  And  panel  from  information  about  players.  This panel is divided into two panels for white and black players. On each of  these  panels  withdrawn  name  player  And  left to him  on  stopwatch time.

public  ChessFrame(ChessClient  parent,  String  user,  Font  fixed)  {  super("Chess  game");

this.user = user;  this.parent  =  parent;

setLayout(new  PackerLayout());  whitePlayer  =  new  Panel();

whiteTime setFont(fixed);  whiteTime.setAlignment(Label.CENTER);  whitePlayer.add("whitename;fill=x;pady=5",  whiteName);  whitePlayer.add("whitetime;fill=x;pady=5",  whiteTime);  blackPlayer  =  new  Panel();

blackPlayer.setLayout(new  PackerLayout());  blackName  =  new  Label(" ");

blackName.setFont(fixed);  blackName.setAlignment(Label.CENTER);  blackTime = new stopWatch();  blackTime.setFont(fixed);  blackTime.setAlignment(Label.CENTER);

blackPlayer.add("blackname;fill=x;pady=5", blackName);  blackPlayer.add("blacktime;fill=x;pady=5", blackTime);  players  =  new  Panel();

players.setLayout(new PackerLayout());  players.add("wplayer;side=bottom;fill=x", whitePlayer);  players.add("bplayer;side=top;fill=x", blackPlayer);  add("panel1;side=left",  players);

board = new ChessBoard();  add("panel2;side=left",  board);  pack();

resize(size());  show();

}

The  frame  handles  only  one  event  -  WINDOWS_DESTROY.  Any  other  event  redirects to the parent object. Thus, the events associated with the moves  players,  transmitted above  and in  eventually fall  to the server:

public  boolean  handleEvent(Event  evt)  {

if (evt.id==Event.WINDOWS_DESTROY) {  dispose();

return  true;

}  else  {

parent.deliverEvent(evt);  return  true;

}

At the time of the initial update of the chessboard, we discover what color  pieces are played by our player. If he plays black, the flipPlayers method will change the labels of the players  in places  and flip the board:

protected  void  flipPlayers()  {  players.remove(whitePlayer);  players.remove(blackPlayer);  players.add("wplayer;side=top;fill=x"  whitePlayer);

players.add("bplayer;side=bottom;fill=x", blackPlayer);  board.setOrientation(false);

}

The following method is the heart of the ChessFrame object - it parses  messages  about  update.  First  at  help  StringTokenizer  we  read  from  this  messages  eight lines of checkerboard status. Next, we determine whose move was (this information  will be used a little later when we determine how much time is left  each player).  Here  fragment  code that implements  this  algorithm:

public  void  updateGame(String  s)  {  System.out.println(s);

st.nextToken();  //  room  games

The following tokens contain the names of the players. If they do not match the names of the players,  indicated in the labels, we assume that the CIS server itself knows what it is doing. If the name  new player in black is the same as our username, and the type variable is not equal to  two  we  turn over  board  so  the way  what  black  turn out  at the bottom.  Variable  type  contains information about the role of a player in a chess game. If it is equal to two, it means that  the user plays in training mode, that is, against himself. If the value  variable is equal to one, which means that the user is playing with a real opponent and in this  moment  his  turn  walk.  IN  any  case  US  required,  to  board  generated  moves:

board.setGenerateMoves(false);

token  =  st.nextToken();  //  time  start  parties

The next two tokens contain the number of seconds left for each of the  players. StopWatches is set to the new, correct time for the player who only  what  done  move,  Countdown  stops  And,  in  my  turn,  starts  counter  another  player:

And finally, we proceed to parse the remaining tokens. In order for the procedure  updates of the chessboard occurred imperceptibly for the user, we perform it in  the very last moment. Each status line is read sequentially,  character by character. If the next character read is a hyphen, the corresponding  the square of the board does not contain a picture; otherwise, the picture is requested from  parental  process:

for  (int  i=0;  i;  i++)  {

if  (ary[j]!='-`)  {

piece  =  parent.getPieceImage(""+ary[j]);

}  else  {

piece  =  null;

}

board.setImage(piece,""+column+row);

}

}

When started, the applet establishes a connection to the server via a socket. For an InputStream object  the corresponding InputStreamHandler is created. public void start() {  try  {

The writeOutput method is used to send data to the server. That this method is  the only one designed for data transmission, gives us two advantages: firstly,  we do not need to repeat the same set of statements at every place in the program where we need to  output data, and secondly, since the synchronized keyword is used in the method,  we have a guarantee that multiple threads of the program will not start transmitting at the same time. IN  early  variable  user  yet  not  assigned  meaning,  but  it  automatically  assigned,  as soon as the first call to writeOutput is made. This is because the first command  serving  on the  server, is the username:

protected  synchronized  void  writeOutput(String  s)  {  if  (user==null)  {

user  =  trim();

}

byte b[] = new byte[s.length()];  s.getBytes(0, s.length(), b, 0);  try  {

ChessOutput.write(b);

}  catch  (IOException  e)  {

handleException(e);

}

}

The receiveInput method is called by the InputStreamHandler object every time the input is received.  complete input string. If the received string is empty or contains only a server prompt,  it is completely ignored. If the received string starts with characters <12>, we know that  it is a signal to update the state of the game - the parseBoard method is called. If  it seems that the line is a signal for the end of the game, its number is analyzed. If number  game is in our hash table, the endGame method of the ChessFrame object is called - and  the corresponding game is removed from the hash table. If the string does not match any of  of the above events, it is regarded as a standard server command and enters the window  extradition  information:

public  void  receiveInput(InputStreamHandler  ish,  Object  o)  {  String  s  =  (String)o;

if  (s.trim().equals("")  ||  s.trim().equals("fics%"))  {  return;

}

if (s.trim().startsWith("<12>")) {  parseBoard(s.trim());

} else if (s.trim().startsWith("{Game")) {  StringTokenizer  st  =  new  StringTokenizer(s);  String token = st.nextToken();  //{Game  String  number  =  st.nextToken();  //number

ChessFrame  frame  =  (ChessFrame)games.get(number);

if  (frame!=null)  {

token  =  st.nextToken();  //(player1  token = st.nextToken();  //vs.  token  =  st.nextToken();  //player2)  token = st.nextToken(); //loser  frame.endGame(token);  games.remove(number);

}

}  else  {

output.appendText(s+"\n");

}

}

The  method  called,  how  only  method  receiveInput  discover  message  about  update  games. The sixteenth field on the line is the game number. If the game is not in our  table, we create a new ChessFrame object and insert its number into the table. Finally we  refresh the window  method  updateGame:

protected void parseBoard(String s) {  StringTokenizer  st  =  new  StringTokenizer(s);  String  token  =  st.nextToken();

if (! token. equals("<12>")) {  output.appendText("oops...  "+ token);

return;

}

for (int i=0; i<<16; i++) {  token  =  st.nextToken();

}

ChessFrame  frame  =  (ChessFrame)games.get(token);  if  (frame==null)  {

frame  =  new  ChessFrame(this,  user,  fixed);  games.put(token,  frame);

}

frame.updateGame(s);

}

# Possible  improvements

Our chess applet has been distributed to the general public and seems to have been well received.  many. As always, advice and recommendations rained down on how it can be  improve. Firstly, the login procedure on the server does not mask the entered password,  therefore, it can be watched by anyone. Second, the applet does not install  board style 12 instead of 1, leaving it up to the player (see Diagram 18-1). Thirdly,  some players found it difficult to keep track of partners ready for multiplayer, that is, they  a separate list of players in a separate window is required. We decided to improve the applet,  releasing its next version.

## Window  login

It was decided to design the login window as a separate, external window. When the user  connects to the server, the applet watches the login window. Once the login window is formed,  the login procedure starts. The login frame consists of two text input fields - one for  name, another for the password - and a button to start the procedure. As a login window, you could  would use a standard dialog since it has the modality property. This means,  that the program does not react to any event that is not related to the dialog itself. Unfortunately,  at the time of writing, the dialog implementation in Netscape Navigator 2.0 for Solaris is  a bit flawed, so we had to do without it. Here is the source code of the class  userlogin:

import java.awt.*;  import  java.util.*;

public  class  UserLogin  extends  frame  {  private  button  login;

private TextField user;  private  TextField  password;  private  Component  target;

The constructor of the UserLogin object specifies the Component object to which to send  event, and sets the font to display in the login window. Next, we add two  TextField text fields, one for the username and one for the password. In the last one  an asterisk (*) is used as the echo character. In addition, we add a login button,  generating  the "login" event and the closing  window:

public UserLogin(Component target, Font f) {  super("Internet  Chess  server  login");

this.target = target;  setBackground(color.gray);  setLayout(new FlowLayout());  Panel p = new Panel();  p.setLayout(new FlowLayout());  label  l  =  new  Label("Username:");  p.add(l);

user  =  new  TextField(16);  user.setFont(f);  user.setEditable(true);  p.add(user);

l  =  new  Label("Password:");  p.add(l);

password = new TextField(16);  password.setFont(f);  password.setEditable(true);  password.setEchoCharacter('*');  p.add(password);

login  =  new  Button("login");  login.setFont(f);  p.add(login);

add(p);

pack();

show();

}

As soon as the user presses the login button, the content of the fields is checked  input - whether anything is entered. If not, we assume the button was pressed.  randomly, and repeat the display of the login window. The password field is not validated because most  chess servers allow everyone to play. If the user entered his name in the window  username , we generate an event and pass it to the object specified earlier when calling  the constructor of the login window. The event parameter is a vector with two elements, the username and  password.  After  Togo  how  event is generated,  window  login  destroyed:

public  boolean  action(Event  evt,  Object  arg)  {  if  (evt.target==login)  {

if  (user.getText().trim().equals(""))  {  return  true;

}

Vector v = new Vector(2);  v.addElement(user.getText());  v.addElement(password.getText());

event  e  =  new  event(this,  Event.ACTION_EVENT,  v);  target.deliverEvent(e);

dispose();  return  true;

}

return  false;

}

This is where the modified part starts. If we wait for the list of players to appear, for  input  lines  created  new  StringTokenizer.  If  line  starts  from  invitations  server,  she doesn't interest us. But if the string starts with the word "Name" - that's what we expect  see. If the next word is "Stand", the rest of the line can be ignored. In any  otherwise, we are dealing with an arbitrary server response and adding it to the output window  TextArea.

Next, we check for the presence and number of hyphens in the next line, and if all  right, completely ignore it. If not, we check if the string starts with a number, beyond  followed by "Players". If yes, the string must be the end of the list of players, so we  update the PlayerFrame and set the waitingforwho variable to false. If none of  the above conditions are not met, the string must be part of the passed list  players, and we parse it, highlighting the player's name and his blitz rating. # the contract

Imagine that some small company asked us to create a system that would  schedule meetings for your employees. These people mostly work for other companies, but  wouldn't mind moving to this company full-time as soon as it gets  sustainable income. They all live in the same area, except for one employee,  moved to another country. With the help of the planner, it will be possible to create your own  schedule  for  everyone  employee  And  alleviate  connection  from  foreign  worker.  This  program  can be written in any language, but it must work on a wide variety of techniques,  because the members of the group are likely to secretly use the equipment of those companies  where they work now. Most users of the system will work in incompatible  networks,  So  what  they  not  will be able  take advantage  existing  commercial  planners.

The task can be simplified by using the Internet and the Java language. Then we  it remains only to write a program that can work on different platforms. Internet  will give the client access to international communications for a very modest fee. Company  invites us to get down to business immediately - in two weeks they want to receive  demo version.

# Properties  planner

The main task of a meeting planner is to help people organize their  time. In addition, it will simplify the scheduling of general meetings by calculating the time  the period in which all members of the group are at work. This program is  a small implementation of popular scheduling software similar to  MeetingMaker or the scheduler that comes with LotusNotes. The difference is that our  the meeting planner will work over the Internet. Most planners work  only on local area networks (LANs) such as Novell. Using the Internet will allow the group  people located on different sides of state borders, use the program in such a way  same  easily,  like this  can be done by a local group  users.

The main feature of the scheduler is its ability to add and cancel appointments.  Therefore, an application for the server and a client must be created, written in the language  Java. This guide will primarily cover the issues of creating a server on  Java.

To eliminate it, we would have to  move  all  data  in  file  to  beginning  And  replace  all  relevant  elements  index  file. This type of operation is common in compression programs and is usually  rarely performed. Disk space is cheap enough that we can afford  our program to run somewhat faster and only periodically perform operations with  database. The code snippet below shows how the find method was executed for  our  schedule stored  on the  disk:

public  scheduleStruct  find(Date  date)

throws  not found exception,  IOException  {  scheduleStruct  result;

long  pos;

Long  conv;

String  key;

String  data;

conv  =  new  Long(date.getTime());  key  =  conv.toString();

key  =  StringUtil.padStringLeft(key,'  ',Size);  data  =  index.findRecord(key);

conv  =  new  Long(data.trim());  pos =  conv.longValue();  return  findPos(pos);

}

public  scheduleStruct  findPos(long  pos)  throws  IOException  {

scheduleStruct  result  =  new  scheduleStruct();  dataFile.seek(pos);

result.start = new Date(dataFile.readLong());  result.end = new Date(dataFile.readLong());  result.desc = new String(dataFile.readLine());  result.descURL = new String(dataFile.readLine());  result.minutesURL  =  new  String(dataFile.readLine());  result.attending = new String(dataFile.readLine());  return  result;

}

This method consists of two subroutines. The first, defined by the schedule interface,  looks through the index file and finds the location of the required element from the file  data. The second subroutine - findPos - is used to recover data from a file  data.  Here  applied  method  readLine.  We  are looking for  relevant  position  And  read  each  field  from  file  data.  Then  these  data  returned to the calling method.

As a result, we come to the last, most difficult subroutine - serversSchedule. To  she  faster  worked  subroutine  findRange  uses  sorted  index  file.

We do two binary searches on the index file to find the start and end  elements. We then loop through each element and find its data in the data file. IN  in the case of a large database and a reasonable range of data, such a procedure is performed  much faster than if you browse the entire database. Now that we have  subroutine to find a specific schedule, we need a subroutine,  returning a range of schedules:

public  scheduleStruct[]  findRange(Date  start,  Date  end)  throws  IOException  {

searchStruct  resultStart,  resultEnd;  Long  conv;

String  key,data;  int  num;

conv  =  new  Long(start.getTime());  key  =  conv.toString();

key  =  StringUtil.padStringLeft(key,'  ',Size);  resultStart  =  index.binarySearch(key);

conv  =  new  Long(end.getTime());  key  =  conv.toString();

key  =  StringUtil.padStringLeft(key,'  ',Size);  resultEnd  =  index.binarySearch(key);

num  =  (int)  (resultEnd.pos  -  resultStart.pos)  /

index.getRecordSize();  if  (num  <  one)  return  null;

scheduleStruct  result[]  =  new  scheduleStruct[num];  int  cnt=0;

for(long  i=resultStart.pos;  i  <  resultEnd.pos;)  {  data  =  index.findPos(i);

// Data is the index in the .dat file  conv  =  new  Long(data.trim());

result[cnt++]  =  findPos(conv.longValue());  i  +=  index.getRecordSize();

}

return  result;

}

}
